clue.text: Huge deficit almost the whole company faces

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut off
to face something is to stand in front of it, so this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
a deficit is a shortfall or loss
the whole of something is all of it

explanation.surface: A firm is staring at an enormous shortfall that wipes out almost everything it has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' is not a verb about confronting the loss; it says the company stands at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal is a straightforward synonym for huge, enormous or gigantic.

clue.text: Worries about son's pet

parts.note: worries are cares
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent frets over their boy's beloved animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like a noun, the son's animal, but it is the verb meaning to stroke fondly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke them affectionately, which is exactly what a caress does.

clue.text: Look into changing application

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: changing the word that follows means rearranging its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to research a change to a job or form application.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is something applied to the skin, so it is an application in the cosmetic sense.

clue.text: Second opinion in the post

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
your take on something is your opinion of it

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a second opinion by letter or in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests mail, but here it is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is a pointed wooden pole driven into the ground, a kind of post.

clue.text: Leaders in athletic tournament induce effort

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
to tempt someone is to induce or entice them

explanation.surface: Those at the top of an athletics competition coax extra effort out of the competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try at something, an effort to achieve it.

clue.text: Orchestra abandoning principal members in Royal Albert Hall upset accompanist?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoning things means leaving them behind, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the principal members of a phrase are the first letters of its words

parts.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An orchestra walks out of a concert, leaving the Royal Albert Hall's performer stranded and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R, A and H from ORCHESTRA to leave OCESTR, then rearrange. The Royal Albert Hall is a famous London concert venue. The question mark flags that this accompanist is not a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone, so it is an accompanist in a non-musical sense, a playful misdirection.

clue.text: Journalists can't supply the first bit of editorial content

parts.note: subs are sub-editors, newspaper journalists

indicators.note: read as 'supple-y', bendy and pliable, so the letters before it are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Reporters are unable to provide even a scrap of an opinion piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but read as an adverb from supple it signals rearranging CANT plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance of something is its content or essential matter, as in the substance of an argument.

clue.text: Pick up extra present for those attending

parts.note: in cricket an over can mean surplus or left over, extra

indicators.note: those attending an event take it in by ear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: present at a roll call means here; it sounds like the verb for listening

explanation.surface: A bonus gift is set aside for the people who come along to an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it means here, as answered at a roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a remark is to catch it by chance, which is what you do when you overhear it.

clue.text: Restrained tense king who wasn't prepared to relinquish line

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: to relinquish something is to give it up, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: the English king Ethelred the Unready
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An anxious king held back from giving up his claim to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred the Unready was a 10th-century English king; drop the L from his name and put T in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up with a rope, so held back or restrained.

clue.text: Takes away cold soup perhaps without coming back

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the result is read backwards
without here means outside, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: soup is an example of a starter, the first course
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A waiter removes a chilled soup without it being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside STARTER after ST, and the whole is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement or offer is to withdraw it, taking it away.

clue.text: Purpose of article

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aim or goal
second meaning: a thing or item

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the aim of a piece of writing; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Object means both an aim, as in the object of the exercise, and a physical thing or item.

clue.text: Unexpected answer held up progress initially

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: ANS is the abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A surprise response stalled the early stages of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap as an adjective means sudden and without warning, as in a snap election.

clue.text: Mouthpiece of bagpipes pokes mandolinist

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters belonging to the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A musician jabs a mandolin player with the part of the bagpipes that is blown into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthpiece' looks like part of the bagpipes, but it is a person who speaks for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is a person who speaks on behalf of another, which is a spokesman's role.

clue.text: I'm amused that man stops where some drive

indicators.note: stops here means plugs, as a stopper fills a gap inside something

parts.note: golfers drive off from the tee
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a man who stops where other people are driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a road, but it is a golf shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle, the sound someone makes to show they are amused.

clue.text: Plant in perfect condition

definitions.meaning: second meaning: as new, like a coin freshly struck

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gardener's note about a healthy plant; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a herb, and an item in mint condition is pristine, as good as new.

clue.text: Football players look forward to meeting of two sides?

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football team
to face is to look forward or towards

explanation.surface: A football team is eager for a match between two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look forward to meeting' reads as a phrase about anticipation, but it splits into a clue piece and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is the boundary where two systems or surfaces meet; the question mark flags the playful wording.

clue.text: Flat fare that provides better features?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin, flat item of food made from batter
second meaning: a thick cosmetic foundation that improves the look of the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' could suggest a ticket price, but it is food; the second half is a cryptic hint at stage make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake is flat batter food, and pancake make-up is a foundation applied to improve facial appearance.

clue.text: Article spreading unorthodox beliefs likely to be accomplished

indicators.note: the letters spread out around a single item, enclosing it
unorthodox means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece spreads heretical ideas that seem quite plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasible means practicable, capable of being done, which is likely to be accomplished.

clue.text: EU work set back discussion

indicators.note: back means in the opposite direction, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that goes is working
set as in placed, like a table laid

explanation.surface: Work on European Union business was delayed by talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation between parties, a discussion.

clue.text: Letter from Scot on vacation in English mansion

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a pile is a grand stately house

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A holidaying Scot sends a letter from a stately home in England.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is British slang for a large imposing house; ST goes inside it, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or literary letter, such as those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Carve piece of sweet chestnut

indicators.note: a piece of the following words is a run of their letters

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a portion of a sweet chestnut tree or nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave or cut lines into a surface, a kind of carving.

clue.text: Worry about paper plates

indicators.note: to plate something is to coat it all over, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious over the crockery made of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' looks like a noun for dishes but is a verb meaning coats.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to worry anxiously.

clue.text: Cool bloke received adoring letters

parts.note: to fan is to cool

indicators.note: received here means heard by a listener, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a bloke is a male; the word sounds like post

explanation.surface: A relaxed man is given letters from admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan mail is the letters a celebrity gets from adoring admirers.

clue.text: Sailor ordered to go somewhere other than this place

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
someone sent away has been ordered to go

explanation.surface: A seaman is commanded to leave for another location.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, so somewhere other than here.

clue.text: Spooner's disheartened and confused woman?

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to lose heart is to lose the middle, so the central letter goes

parts.note: the name itself, taken as written

explanation.surface: It looks like a spoonerism of some depressed, bewildered woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' promises a spoonerism, but the name is the fodder: remove its middle O to get SPONER, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman is an example of a human being; the question mark signals definition by example.

clue.text: Two notes produced by reporter from The Sun

indicators.note: a reporter speaking aloud on air makes the words sound, so spelling follows the sound

parts.note: soh and lah are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A journalist on The Sun newspaper produces a couple of brief memos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which makes 'reporter' feel natural, but the sun is the star. In a non-rhotic accent the two notes sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or coming from the sun.

clue.text: Artist who has an arresting power?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the English landscape painter John ...
second meaning: a police officer, who can arrest people

explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' suggests striking art, tying the two halves together, but it means making arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable painted The Hay Wain, and a constable is a police officer with powers of arrest.

clue.text: What may join group of players up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: It asks who might sign up to a band of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join' suggests joining a band, but it is woodworking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting piece of wood that fits into a mortise to join two parts.

clue.text: Bishop mocked endlessly about being short of money

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or mock them

explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a creature who has no money.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is a person with no money who asks others for it, a being who is penniless.

clue.text: Unfortunate lapses during breaks causing no problems

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
in means during, as in in the night

explanation.definitionFit: Painless means without pain or difficulty, so causing no trouble.

clue.text: One plus one is prime

parts.note: surface reading: simple arithmetic, one plus one equals two, the first prime
setter's reading: the digit one written beside another one makes a two-digit prime number

explanation.walkthrough: The sum suggests two, but 'plus' means placing the digits side by side, giving 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Two ones written together make the number 11, which is a prime number.

clue.text: Factory working round clock ultimately makes school food

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A factory works round the clock to produce school dinners.
